title: Dates limit what can cause what
statement: Treat dates as limits on cause: mark each period, count a date usable only when its position matters to an argument, and use later events only for change or significance.
example: A unit ending in 1607 had records carrying later events, which made items look plausible while testing the next unit.
detail: An AP history course's design document calls chronology a reasoning constraint: dates bound what can cause what, and context may reach outside a prompt's period only if the response explains the relationship instead of smuggling later knowledge into the claim. It marks period boundaries on every lesson and assessment object and teaches three uses of time: evidence from inside the period, prior context, and later consequence only when the prompt calls for change over time or significance. Because students often know events as isolated cards, it builds timelines around what existed before, what operated during and what followed, and counts a date usable when the student can explain why its position matters to an argument. The course's audit of inherited records found a unit's records carrying events from after its end date, and ruled that later context be labelled and never required for the key.
